input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer (15% of annual Fees per week of delay, after only a ten-day grace), which breaches the preferred position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer and, compounding weekly, would rapidly exceed the remaining contract value (walk-away territory). Other Customer-payable amounts are compliant: Section 9.4 limits termination liability to accrued Fees with no early-termination fee, Section 27 termination is "without penalty", and the Section 21 cap contains no penalty/LD carve-out. Preferred remedy is deletion; simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts is an acceptable substitute.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the late-payment liquidated damages in Section 7.7, as our playbook does not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us; 15% of annual Fees per week is punitive and unrelated to any actual loss. If Vendor needs a late-payment remedy, we can accept simple interest at a commercially reasonable rate on undisputed overdue amounts.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment (Section 7.7).
